evidence: No known CRITICAL or HIGH advisory applies to any dependency reachable from the repo's entry points at the scanned commit
expected_output: Gated advisory rows: advisory, severity, package, version, ecosystem, reachable (true|false|unknown), not_affected, path (the call path as the artifact); openvex.json with a not_affected statement per proven-unreachable advisory

assertions.description: Zero CRITICAL or HIGH advisories reachable — or of unknown reachability — from the repo's entry points.

notes: M4 posture: reachability-gated. An advisory is not_affected only when the code graph PROVES the package is beyond every entry point and declared route — that claim is emitted as OpenVEX with justification vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path. No graph, or no detectable entry points, degrades to the M1 posture: every advisory counts, marked unknown.

plain.checks: Cross-references the repository's component inventory against published advisories, then walks the code to see whether the affected package can be reached at all from the places the program starts.
plain.violation: A dependency with a known critical or high-severity advisory sits on a path your code can execute — or the walk could not prove that it does not, which counts the same way here. This is the subset worth your attention, not the whole advisory list.
plain.fix: Upgrade the named package to the fixed version the finding states. Where no fix has been published, the remaining move is to remove the path that reaches it; unreachability is a claim this system will only make from the code graph, never from an assurance.
